gpu_vlm.name: Qwen3-VL 8B (INT8)
gpu_vlm.notes: Verified 2026-06-16 on Arc 140V in dual mode (NPU text + GPU vision): correct color/shape ID, ~6s. INT8 retains OCR/number detail better than INT4 at ~9 GB; fits a 16 GB ARC. One generation behind Qwen3.5, but the most thoroughly verified GPU vision pairing for Qwen3-8B on NPU.

gpu_vlm.name: Gemma 4 26B-A4B (INT4)
gpu_vlm.notes: The power pick IF your GPU has XMX (Arc/Lunar Lake — install.ps1 says so above): multimodal MoE (128 experts), 26.6 tok/s on Arc 140V, 21.0 on a 24-core CPU, 262k context. Will NOT load on non-XMX iGPUs. Verified 2026-08-09 on Arc B390: 14.3 GB of weights does NOT fit a 16.4 GB GPU budget — it fails with a CL_INVALID_EVENT/ProgramBuilder error, which is OOM wearing a driver error's clothes. Use --offload-ratio: ratio 10 gives 18.2 tok/s decode / 3.1s TTFT (ratio 30 drops to 15.6/4.0, so use the SMALLEST ratio that loads). Vision verified under offload. Keep the ASR model off the GPU when running this.

gpu_vlm.name: Gemma 4 E4B (INT4)
gpu_vlm.notes: Verified 2026-08-09 on Arc B390 (Panther Lake, XMX): 24.7 tok/s decode, 3.1s TTFT via benchmark.py — faster than Qwen3-8B on that machine's NPU (18.6 tok/s, 4.7s TTFT). Coherent English, vision correct on a screenshot. 131k context, 84 KB/token KV. INT4 asymmetric g128 per rt_info. Do NOT run on NPU (garbage or 0.1 tok/s — see TODONT.md).

gpu_vlm.name: Gemma 4 E4B (INT8)
gpu_vlm.notes: Runs on every device class except NPU: 16.4 tok/s on Arc 140V, ~13 on CPU and non-XMX iGPU. Verified 2026-08-07, lightly. Prefer the INT4 above unless you need the quality headroom. Do NOT run on NPU (garbage or 0.1 tok/s — see TODONT.md).

gpu_vlm.name: Qwen3.5 4B (INT4)
gpu_vlm.notes: Newest Qwen VLM generation (Qwen2.5-VL -> Qwen3-VL -> Qwen3.5). Verified on Arc 140V 2026-08-07: 27 tok/s VLM streaming. Reads text in images well but confidently invents product identities from logos — prompt for visible features only.

gpu_vlm.name: Qwen3-VL 8B (INT4)
gpu_vlm.notes: Recommended. One generation behind Qwen3.5. Verified on Xe-LPG iGPU for OCR, color/count, no hallucination on empty input. Like all VLMs, prone to confident hallucination on ambiguous images (e.g., invented make/model/year from unbadged photos) — prompt for visible features only and ask for uncertainty explicitly.

gpu_vlm.name: Qwen2.5-VL 3B (INT8)
gpu_vlm.notes: Recommended (proven). INT8 retains fine detail (OCR, numbers) better than INT4. Research license (non-commercial) — see model card.

gpu_vlm.name: Qwen3.5 9B (INT4)
gpu_vlm.notes: Experimental. Qwen3.5 generation, natively multimodal (image-text-to-text) — full VLM on GPU. Untested here; needs OpenVINO 2026.2+.

gpu_vlm.name: Gemma 3 12B Vision (INT4)
gpu_vlm.notes: Untested. Needs ~12 GB RAM with KV cache.

gpu_vlm.name: Gemma 4 E2B Vision (INT4)
gpu_vlm.notes: Untested. Google Gemma 4 — efficient (E2B effective-2B) successor to Gemma 3. Needs OpenVINO 2026.2+.

whisper.name: Whisper Base (INT8)
whisper.notes: Fastest. Multi-language. Pre-exported — no conversion step (just a small, quick download).

whisper.name: Whisper Small (INT8)
whisper.notes: Good balance. Multi-language. Pre-exported — no conversion step (small, quick download).

whisper.name: Whisper Medium (INT8)
whisper.notes: Best accuracy under 16 GB. Multi-language. Pre-exported — no conversion step (download still needed).

gpu_llm.name: Qwen3-Coder 30B-A3B (INT4)
gpu_llm.notes: Verified on Arc B390 (Panther Lake, XMX), 2026-08-10: 15.2 GB int4, 128 experts / 8 active, 262k model context, 96 KB/token KV. Needs a GPU with XMX -- auto disk offload is what makes it fit an 18.5 GB budget. Measured steady-state: 32k context (pool 3 GB, auto ratio 15%) 21.2 tok/s, TTFT 1.15s warm; 87k context (pool 8 GB, auto ratio 49%) 12.8 tok/s, TTFT 5.8s. Tool calling and sequential requests both verified through the serving path. Raise the iGPU Shared Memory Override to ~25 GB to drop the ratio to 0 and keep both.

gpu_llm.name: Qwen2.5-Coder 14B (INT4)
gpu_llm.notes: Recommended for VS Code Copilot Chat / tool calling (--vscode-compat). Fits 16GB with KV headroom. Emits Hermes-style <tool_call> JSON, handled by parse_tool_calls. Prefer Qwen3-Coder 30B-A3B on an XMX GPU (disk offload makes it fit and it is faster); this remains the best coder for non-XMX GPUs, where offload is a no-op.

gpu_llm.name: Qwen2.5-Coder 7B (INT4)
gpu_llm.notes: Lighter Copilot/tool-calling option. Faster than the 14B, weaker on multi-step agent loops. Same Hermes tool-call format.

gpu_llm.name: Qwen3.6 27B (INT4)
gpu_llm.notes: Untested. Newest generation, natively multimodal. ~16 GB int4 — borderline on a 16 GB Arc, may fall back to CPU silently like the 30B-A3B. Needs OpenVINO 2026.2+.

gpu_llm.name: Qwen3 30B-A3B MoE (INT4)
gpu_llm.notes: Best quality. Needs >32 GB RAM (shared with system). Verified 2026-08-09 on 285K CPU via CB backend (smoke test). 262k context — holds a whole novel with --cache-size-gb 12.

gpu_llm.name: Qwen3 Thinking 30B-A3B MoE (INT4)
gpu_llm.notes: Always-thinking sibling of the Instruct 30B-A3B, same int4 recipe (our export — no Intel pre-export exists). Verified 2026-08-09 on 285K CPU: multi-step reasoning then a correct answer. Output ends thinking with </think> (no opening tag); give it max_tokens headroom or the reasoning eats the budget.

gpu_llm.name: Qwen3 Coder 30B-A3B MoE (INT4)
gpu_llm.notes: Code-focused MoE. Needs >32 GB RAM (shared with system).
